summary: A WordPress/Divi one-pager (captured via Wayback) for Optician Sans, a free display face built from Snellen and Sloan eye-chart optotypes: a black hero whose giant 'O' pulses in and out of focus like an eye test, a promo video, press quotes, a LogMAR chart, a Snellen → Sloan → Optician Sans lineage of single letters on grids, the alphabet as an eye-chart grid, an alternates table and a black licensing/contact footer.

instances.look: Black field: left 'OPTICIAN SANS' in white caps, a three-line tagline, an outlined 'DOWNLOAD FOR FREE ▸' button and a row of award badges (One Show, TDC, Communication Arts, ED Awards, Gullblyanten); right a single huge white 'O' that blurs and sharpens
instances.feel: Calm, clever, like looking into an eye-test machine
instances.ux: The 'O' loops between blurred and sharp (CSS filter blur 10px → 0) like an eye focusing; the button downloads the ZIP directly
instances.learn: Animate the one glyph with the theme's own effect (out-of-focus → sharp for an eye-chart font): a single CSS filter carries the whole concept

reconstruction.layout: Full-bleed 1440×570px black, two equal columns; left column text block from x≈116, name at y≈160, tagline 440px wide, button 316×50px, badges row ~50px tall ~240px wide; right column a ~360px 'O' centred at x≈1080
reconstruction.typography: Name ~44px Optician Sans Regular caps, tracked +0.05em, white; tagline ~22px Montserrat Regular, leading 1.4; button ~17px caps tracked +0.1em, 2px white border
reconstruction.behaviour: @keyframes optics { from { filter: blur(10px) } to { filter: blur(0) } } looping alternate on the O image (~3s); text modules fade in from the top ('fadeTop') on load
reconstruction.content: Tagline 'A free font based on the historical eye charts and optotypes used by opticians world wide.'
reconstruction.assets: Big 'O' image or glyph; award badge strip image (Sertificates@2x)

instances.look: Under the hero's download button, a small cluster of award badges: The One Show, TDC Certificate of Excellence, Communication Arts Award of Excellence, then ED Awards and Gullblyanten 2015 logos
instances.learn: Tuck award badges right under the free-download button: social proof at the moment of decision

reconstruction.layout: One image ~240×100px, two rows of logos below the button in the left hero column

instances.look: A wide embedded YouTube video ('Optician Sans - new free font') on black, extending from the hero's black band into the white page below; the capture shows only a black player with a play button
instances.ux: Click to play the promo film
instances.learn: Let the video frame straddle the black hero and the white page: it bridges the two sections

reconstruction.layout: Black band ~330px continues below the hero, then white; the video (1080×~610px, 16:9) is centred at x=180–1260 and straddles the black/white edge, ~45px white margin below

instances.look: Two rows of three press quotes on white, each a tiny italic tracked caps headline ('"WEIRD AND WONDERFUL"', '"EN ELEGANT TYPEFACE"', '"LET`S EVERYONE ACT AS A OPTICIAN"', '"COMPLETES THE EYE TEST CHART ALPHABET"'…) above the outlet's logo (Gizmodo, Fast Company, NRK, Dezeen, designmodo, Khoi Vinh / Adobe), rows split by a grey rule
instances.learn: Quote only the headline each outlet ran, in small caps above its logo: press proof in one glance

reconstruction.layout: Content width ~680px centred, 3 equal columns, row height ~150px; 1px #b0b0b0 rule between rows
reconstruction.typography: Quotes ~9px Optician Sans italic caps, tracked +0.05em; logos ~22px tall

instances.look: Left, a short paragraph on the LogMAR chart (10 letters, National Vision Research Institute of Australia); right, a LogMAR chart in the font: rows 'C O H Z V', 'S Z N D C', 'V K C N R'… shrinking to a point
instances.learn: Set the real-world source artefact (the eye chart) in the new font: the reference and the specimen are the same picture

reconstruction.layout: Two columns: paragraph 330px wide at x≈80, vertically centred; chart ~280px wide at x≈550 (×2 on the 1440 page ≈ x 1100), 11 rows decreasing from ~40px to ~6px
reconstruction.typography: Paragraph ~14px Open Sans Regular, leading 1.6, dark grey; chart letters Optician Sans caps, tracked widely, black
reconstruction.content: Real facts about the LogMAR chart

instances.look: On light grey, three letters side by side on faint construction grids: a slab-serif 'E' (SNELLEN – 1862 –), a sans 'D' (SLOAN – 1959 –) and a 'K' (OPTICIAN SANS – 2018 –) with two grey dots marking the optical corrections, each with a title, italic date and a short centred caption
instances.learn: Draw one letter from each ancestor on the same grid: the lineage reads left to right without a timeline graphic

reconstruction.layout: Full-width 1440×896 band #e5e5e5; three columns centred at x≈360, 720, 1080; each grid box ~250×240px with ~25px cells in #c8c8c8 hairlines, glyph ~165px tall; title 70px below, date, then 4–5 line caption ~260px wide
reconstruction.typography: Titles ~20px Optician Sans caps, tracked; dates ~13px Georgia italic grey; captions ~14px Montserrat/Open Sans grey #888, centred, leading 1.6
reconstruction.content: Real history: Snellen 1862 (5×5 grid), Sloan 1959 (10 letters), Optician Sans 2018 (optically adjusted display face)

instances.look: Split band: left black half with a blue vertical rule and a white quote ('The typeface, made with Sloan optotypes as the basis of construction, is the most effective letter selection…') signed Øyvind Krogh, Optometrist at Optiker-A; right half a portrait photo of the bearded optometrist in glasses on blue-grey
instances.learn: Get the endorsement from the profession the font imitates (an optometrist), with his portrait: domain authority beats design press

reconstruction.content: Real customer quote (the font was commissioned for an optician's identity)

instances.look: The capital alphabet A–Z as a 6-column grid of big black letters on white, widely spaced like an eye chart (D, G, U and Z are missing in the desktop capture: their images failed to load from the Wayback copy)
instances.learn: Space a caps-only display alphabet like an eye chart, one letter per wide cell: the grid itself recalls the source
